sa_market_summary: The Ford Ranger is South Africa's second best-selling vehicle and the Hilux's closest rival. Built at Ford's Silverton plant in Pretoria, making it a locally assembled product with strong parts support. The T6 platform (2011-2022) established the Ranger's reputation for toughness and payload capability. The next-generation Ranger (2022+) upgraded technology significantly. The 3.2 TDCi five-cylinder diesel is regarded as one of the most robust engines in the bakkie segment. Excellent choice for both work and leisure.

known_faults.fault: EGR valve failure (2.2 TDCi and 3.2 TDCi)
known_faults.description: EGR (Exhaust Gas Recirculation) valve failure is a common maintenance item on both 2.2 and 3.2 TDCi Rangers. Symptoms include rough idle, black smoke, and reduced power.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check for black exhaust smoke at idle. Request an EGR cleaning or replacement history. A scan tool will reveal EGR fault codes.
known_faults.source: Ford SA dealer reports, SA Ranger owners forums, AutoTrader SA buyer guides

known_faults.description: Manual transmission Rangers use a dual mass flywheel that wears at higher mileage, particularly under heavy towing or off-road use. A rattling or shuddering on startup/shutdown is a classic symptom.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Listen for a rattle from the gearbox area on startup and shutdown. Feel for shudder on clutch engagement. Request clutch and DMF replacement history.
known_faults.source: SA Ranger forum, Ford SA dealer service records, SA gearbox workshops

known_faults.description: The 2.2 TDCi water pump has a known weak point in the impeller shaft seal. Coolant leaks and overheating result if not caught early.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check for coolant level drops. Inspect hose connections for white residue indicating a seeping water pump. Replace proactively on high mileage examples.
known_faults.source: Ford SA technical service bulletins, SA diesel specialist reports

known_faults.description: The 6-speed manual gearbox synchros wear at high mileage, causing crunching when changing into second and third gear. Aggressive driving or overloading accelerates wear.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Test downshift into second gear under normal driving. Any crunching or resistance points to synchromesh wear.
known_faults.source: SA gearbox specialist workshops, Ranger owners forum

known_faults.description: Rangers used for overloading, constant heavy towing, or severe off-road use can develop hairline chassis cracks around the rear crossmember. This is a safety issue.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Physical underbody inspection with a flashlight around the rear crossmember and body mounts. Particularly important for ex-fleet, farm, or construction vehicles.
known_faults.source: SA 4x4 forum, Ford SA chassis inspection bulletins

what_to_inspect_before_buying: Underbody inspection for chassis cracks ,  non-negotiable on commercial-use bakkies
Check EGR condition with a diagnostic scan
For manual transmissions, test clutch engagement and listen for DMF rattle
Confirm water pump replacement history on 2.2 TDCi models above 80,000km
Test 4WD system engagement and transfer case operation
Check for rust on chassis and load bay floor
Request full Ford SA service history
Inspect canopy or accessories for quality and secure fitment
owner_sentiment: Very positive. Ranger owners value the combination of work capability and on-road comfort. 3.2 TDCi owners particularly loyal to the five-cylinder engine. Main concerns are EGR maintenance costs and DMF expense on high-mileage manual examples. The 2.0 BiTurbo models (2019+) are praised for performance but some owners report higher servicing costs.
